article.title: Our newest AI Quest: Mapping the human brain

harvestedTerms.summary: Google launches 'Polar Peaks,' the third in its AI Quests series — an interactive educational game for ages 11–14 that teaches AI literacy through a neuroscience/brain-mapping scenario, developed with Stanford. The article announces accompanying teacher training modules via the Google AI Educator Series. The piece is primarily a product/program announcement with light educational-methodology content.

article.title: Is HR Tech Undermining Your Strategy?

harvestedTerms.summary: MIT Sloan Management Review article on HR technology strategy, arguing that vendor-default HR platforms undermine organizational strategy through 'accumulation trap' dynamics. The piece introduces a 'Strategy-First Check-In' framework for aligning HR tech stacks to talent management priorities. Minimal AI-specific terminology; primarily a management/strategy piece with light AI context.

Ben Thompson's 'The End of the Internet' traces the full arc of the open web — from blogs to social media to SEO to AI — arguing that each phase ends when infinite supply destroys discovery value, and that aggregators (Google, then social, now AI) capture the value created by open content while hollowing out the creators. The piece extends Thompson's Aggregator Theory into the AI era, arguing AI assistants now disintermediate even the aggregators, ending the web as a distribution channel and raising foundational questions about content creation incentives.

mustReadFlagged.reason: One of the clearest long-form arguments that AI assistants are not just another wave of internet change but represent a structural endpoint — the final aggregation layer that breaks the incentive chain that made open web publishing viable. Thompson traces this thesis through his own twenty-year publishing history, making it both analytically rigorous and unusually concrete. Essential reading for anyone trying to understand how AI reshapes the information ecosystem, not just its products.

article.title: The RealReal won’t let AI agents hog designer clothing

harvestedTerms.summary: The RealReal updates its bot-defense system after The Verge demonstrated that Meta's Muse AI agent could exploit its shopping cart reserve system to effectively block other consumers from purchasing luxury items for hours. The article surfaces real-world friction emerging as AI agents become mainstream shopping tools, touching on agentic commerce, bot defenses, and the disruption to retail business models as agents mediate consumer-web interactions.
